scope: Userdata characterization for FUN_00d11400's metatable (cataloged structurally in BCS-Y-0502). Goal: identify the C++ type the userdata wraps and the semantic role it serves. Method: full decomp of all 6 distinct metamethod impls + the wrapping cclosure (_isAlive) + both static callers.
outcome: Userdata wraps an Individual Reference handle - a 2-dword (GroupID, IndividualIndex) entity addressing pattern. Constructor `__lge_getIndividualIndex(group, index)` packs the 2 args; the only Lua-side method exposed is `_isAlive()` (calls FUN_00ce19c0 for engine-side alive-check). All 8 arithmetic operators are no-ops (FUN_00d10ef0 returns 1, does nothing) - allowing scripts to do `idx + 1` syntax for iteration without erroring.

fields.name: group_id
fields.notes: First dword. Likely the group identifier in FFXIV's group-scoped addressing (party / linkshell / zone / content). Compared in __eq.

fields.name: individual_index
fields.notes: Second dword. Likely the per-group entity index. Compared in __eq.

luaUserdataLayout.outerSizeNote: Lua userdata body holds a single pointer to the 8-byte inner struct (per __gc destructor which calls _free(*puVar4) on the dereferenced pointer).

__index.behavior: Hard-coded 9-byte string compare against "_isAlive". On match: push FUN_00d11010 as cclosure (the alive-check method). On non-match: fall through to security-cookie no-op. This metatable exposes EXACTLY ONE METHOD to Lua scripts.

__newindex.behavior: No-op (security-cookie placeholder). Userdata is effectively read-only.

__eq.behavior: Dword-by-dword compare of the 2 inner-struct fields. Two IndividualRef userdata are equal iff both group_id and individual_index match.

__gc.behavior: Pool-recycled destructor. Looks up a pool at offset +0x21c of a context structure (probably the LuaState env). If pool has room (< 0x200 entries by computed (end - begin) >> 2), recycle the inner struct back into the pool via FUN_00d1fff0. Otherwise direct _free.

constructors.name: __lge_getIndividualIndex
constructors.implNotes: Takes 2 Lua number args, converts each to int via FUN_009d6600 (double-to-int), creates a new userdata at stack slot 3 via FUN_00cd77d0, then calls FUN_00d11400 to install the metatable + write the 2 dwords. The decompiler's local_10 = uVar1 | iVar2 >> 0x1f expression is the 64-bit packing artifact - the actual stored value is (group_id, individual_index).

constructors.name: FUN_00d2b810
constructors.implNotes: 6-arg internal constructor. Takes a context struct (param_1, accessed at +0x14 and +0x2c), a description (param_2..param_6), then constructs an IndividualRef userdata at param_3's slot via FUN_00d11400. Special-cases DAT_0130d78c and DAT_0130d79c as invalid/wildcard markers (when present, computes iVar2 = -1 instead of *param_5 * iVar5 + *param_6). Used by some engine internal path - not a Lua N-API.

exposedMethods.name: _isAlive
exposedMethods.implNotes: Gets the inner pointer from the userdata (puVar4 = userdata; *puVar4 = inner_struct_ptr), then calls FUN_00ce19c0(state, inner_ptr) and pushes the boolean result. FUN_00ce19c0 is the engine-side alive-check that reads the 2 dwords of the inner struct.

ffxiv1xInterpretation: The (group_id, individual_index) shape matches FFXIV 1.x's well-documented group-scoped entity addressing system. Groups in FFXIV 1.x include: party, linkshell, retainer, area entity table, content groups, etc. The 'Individual' terminology aligns with the binary's `__lge_*` LGE engine namespace and matches the way Lua scripts in client-data reference entities. This userdata is the bridge between Lua scripts and the engine's group/individual addressing scheme. _isAlive returning false probably indicates the entity has been removed from its group (e.g., NPC despawned, player logged out, retainer dismissed).
